caption: Figure 1. Schematic of Probabilistic Risk Intelligence for Safe Mission Planning (PRISM). Current sensor tracks are mapped to three unlabeled future branches with mixture probabilities and time-varying positional uncertainty. Forecast centers enter candidate feasibility checks, while an uncertainty-dependent risk field contributes to path ranking in a fixed planner. Branch probabilities and path shapes are illustrative.

Figure 2. Traffic-simulation, dataset, and evaluation pipeline. Training, validation, in-distribution (ID) test, and out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation episodes are generated independently. Constant-velocity (CV) extrapolation is a pre-training dataset diagnostic, and repeated branch rollouts provide simulator-state-conditioned futures for assessing the forecast distribution. The predictor receives sensor observations only.

Figure 3. Simulated avoidance response in a nearly head-on encounter. Arrows show travel direction; the black dashed and green solid lines trace the ownship and fixed-wing UAS intruder trajectories, respectively. The green and orange circles mark first detection and turn onset. The gray dotted line extrapolates the intruder's pre-turn velocity without a turn. The gray and orange connectors mark minimum separations of 84 and 482 m for the no-turn and simulated turned paths, respectively.

Figure 4. PRISM predictor architecture. The 10 × 20 × 13 observation tensor is processed by feature embedding, a temporal Transformer, attention pooling, and an inter-object Transformer before branching into trajectory-distribution, mixture-weight, and auxiliary class heads. The network is shared across targets and applied in batch.

Figure 5. Integration architecture. An observation-only forecast is converted to time-indexed planning disks. Their centers and hard radii enter the fixed planner's feasibility screen, while mixture weight and scale determine the soft-risk score. Dashed consumers are outside the present evaluation.

Figure 6. Schematic of risk-aware candidate selection in Frenet coordinates. In (a), paths are evaluated near an illustrative risk contour; in (b), the selected path is emphasized and the others fade.

Figure 7. PRISM (a, c, e) and observed-track CV (b, d, f) for two eVTOL corridor cases and one unseen search-wandering object. Branch width denotes mixture weight. Blue shading is the 0–15 s sweep of HPD regions; outlines mark 5, 10, and 15 s, and gray traces show 60 futures. These are predictive distributions, not collision probabilities.

Figure 8. State-conditioned rollout calibration. Panels (a–c) show HPD coverage for ID, raw OOD, and scaled OOD; (e–g) show 15 s density-PIT diagnostics. Each condition has 60 futures. Panel (d) audits old versus corrected timing for the submitted oracle-association checkpoint, not the retrained model. The OOD scale T = 1.695 was fitted on disjoint episodes.

Figure 9. Class-wise prediction from 10 s tracks. (a) ID auxiliary-head confusion. (b) ID minADE against observed CV, corrected IMM, and true-state CV (oracle). (c) ID 90% HPD coverage by horizon. (d) OOD errors, with unseen classes shaded and their dominant trained-class assignments indicated. Bars are episode-cluster bootstrap intervals.

Figure 10. OOD-fitted uncertainty scaling and transfer. The multiplier T = 1.695 is fitted on 300 episodes and tested unchanged on 900 disjoint episodes and factor-wise shifts. Panels show 15 s nominal 90% coverage and marginal NLL. Improved held-out OOD coverage does not imply uniform transfer.

Figure 11. One-factor OOD tests of the fixed planner checkpoint. Density, wind, intent, and platform mix are changed separately; the last set changes all factors. Panels show minADE, 15 s nominal 90% coverage, and class accuracy. The source reports provide point estimates without intervals.

Figure 12. PRISM episode 319 at t = 17.5 s. Magenta shows the remaining plan issued at 16.0 s. Dark blue is the selected 13 s plan; light-blue dashes show actual flight to 44.3 s under repeated replanning. Gray paths are the other 97 feasible candidates; 177 candidates failing corridor or dynamic limits are omitted. Maps summarize the next 15 s and omit upper-scene traffic only for display; planning used all traffic. The bird contributes 97% of the selected plan's soft safety cost. Spatial overlap in the swept maps does not establish a simultaneous collision.

Figure 13. Closed-loop rate ratios across five settings. Squares show CV/PRISM and circles static/PRISM; above one favors PRISM. Panel (a) counts union encounters below 152.4 m; (b) counts contiguous union runs directly below 76.2 m; (c) counts 152.4 m union encounters whose unrounded minimum separation is below 45 m. Panels (a–c) use the corrected current-track screen. In these panels, bars are exploratory paired-episode 95% bootstrap intervals, unadjusted for multiplicity. Panel (d) shows unscreened time below 45 m per exposure hour. All 152.4 m CV/PRISM intervals include one.

Figure 14. Common-hard-geometry control on the first 300 nominal OOD pairs. Filled markers use arm-specific forecast disks; open markers use shared observed-position disks with arm-specific soft risk. Panels (a, b) show event rates and (c, d) paired ratios, where above one favors the denominator. Severe events are 152.4 m union encounters whose unrounded minimum separation is below 45 m; event counts use the corrected current-track screen. Bars are exploratory paired-episode 95% bootstrap intervals, unadjusted for multiplicity. The control probes feasibility effects but does not decompose the 600-pair result (Table S6).

Figure 15. Nominal 90% coverage offline and for forecasts generated and logged during closed-loop operation in the first 300 episodes per nominal-ID and nominal-OOD arm. Panels show pooled estimates and strata defined by ownship maneuver or intruder reaction within the subsequent 15 s window, evaluated at 5, 10, and 15 s. These future-derived strata are descriptive. CV under-covers substantially. Figure 17 adds the 50% and 70% levels and the stratum with neither ownship maneuver nor intruder reaction.

Figure 16. Subsequent flight in the encounter introduced in Figure 12, under static (A), CV (B), and PRISM (C). The selected bird's path differs by less than 30 m across arms; closest bird separation is 11.2, 27.2, and 221.8 m. A separate GA aircraft reaches 20.4, 3.1, and 37.7 m, so PRISM does not avoid all hazards. Later traffic may diverge; the example explains the route change, while Tables 11 and 11b compare planning outcomes across episodes.

Figure 17. HPD coverage for forecasts generated and logged during the first 300 episodes per nominal-ID and nominal-OOD arm, at nominal 50%, 70%, and 90% levels and 5, 10, and 15 s, with offline test-set coverage shown for reference. Ownship-maneuver and intruder-reaction strata use the subsequent 15 s window and are not available at forecast time. PRISM uses 256 Monte Carlo draws per point; CV is analytic. Points are descriptive estimates without episode-bootstrap intervals. Table S9 reports sample counts and inclusion rules.

Figure 18. Reacquisition errors for current-track models (diamonds) and oracle association (stars), paired by episode, forecast time, and agent. Bars are 95% episode-cluster intervals. An earlier closed track lies within 10 s in reacquisition cases but is not used by the revised model.

Figure 19. Validation NLL (top) and minADE (bottom) for current-track models; circles mark retained epochs. Point-MSE is excluded from NLL because its spread head was untrained. The 1× and 5× models use different validation sets; Table 10 compares them on common test samples.

Figure 20. One-factor planning sensitivity on the first 300 nominal OOD pairs. CV/PRISM ratios above one favor PRISM. Rows vary the scale floor, plateau, safety weight, normalization, pruning, or isotropic reduction, while encounter thresholds and the corrected current-track screen remain fixed. Panel (a) counts 152.4 m union encounters; panel (b) counts those whose unrounded minimum separation is below 45 m. Bars are exploratory 95% paired-episode bootstrap intervals, unadjusted for multiplicity; PRISM-only rows reuse baseline CV episodes.
Figure 21. Fixed-checkpoint sensitivity to maneuver dwell, perception probability, and sensor noise. Panels show minADE, marginal NLL, and 15 s nominal 90% coverage without confidence intervals.
